Pawan Kumar on 7 May, 2016 In The Court Of Ms.Pooja Aggarwal: Metropolitan Magistrate02: Mahila Court:South District: Saket Court: New Delhi Cc No: 13/1 (07.01.2015) Unique Case Id: 02406R0005502015 Jurisdiction of Police Station: Sangam Vihar Smt. Lalita, W/o Sh. Pawan Kumar, D/o Sh. Mohan Lal, R/o J1st , H.No. 164/11, Near Neem Chawk, Veer Bazar, Sangam Vihar, New Delhi110062. ..........Agg Versus 1.Sh. Pawan Kumar, S/o Sh. Pyare Lal, 2.Sh. texts.facts: 1. By way of the present application under Section 12 of the Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005, Smt. Lalita (hereinafter referred to as "the aggrieved'') has sought various reliefs against her husband and parents in law (hereinafter referred as "the respondents") including Protection CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors. Page 1 order under Section 18, Residence Order under Section 19, Monetary relief under Section 20, Compensation order under section 22 of the Act. 2. As per the aggrieved she married the respondent no.1 on 13.03.2013 at Kanyadan Mahadan Vivah Sammelan, Gandhi Harijan Vidyalaya, Dakshinpuri, Dr. Ambedkar Nagar as per Hindu rites and customs in which several gifts were given to the parties and after her marriage she stayed with the respondents. The aggrieved states that in the month of April, 2013, the respondents started taunting her for insufficient dowry including less gifts regarding the less gifts/articles/ cash and Marriage Video etc. and when she expressed inability of her parents to fulfill their demands, they abused her and warned her to go to her parent's house with her luggage and also took all her jewellery. She has stated that she was subjected to comments and taunts in all her daily activities e.g. eating, sitting, sleeping etc. caused her mental harassment. 4. She has further stated that one day, the respondents pressurized her to arrange a two wheeler vehicle for the respondent no.1 and cash amount Rs. 1 lakh from her parents and if she did not do so she will be thrown out and when she objected she was beaten by them. She has further stated that since her marriage, she has been subjected to regular abuse and beatings by respondent no.1 who also pressurize her to work for living and also threatened to kill her if she disclosed about their torture to anybody including the neighbours or her parents. 5. She has also stated that after marriage she came to know ab respondent no.1 being a habitual drunker with the habit of eating Gutka and CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors. Page 2 of 1 that he used to spend his money on drinking and gambling and also beat her when she objected. She has further stated that respondent no. 1 used to snatch all her money and also pressurized her to fulfill their demands of Rupees One Lakh in cash and two wheeler vehicle and upon her inability threatened to kill her and threw her out of the house. She has further stated on 09.10.2013, she made a complaint at Mahila Panchayat where the respondents were called and matter was compromised and she was sent back with the respondents on their assurance of keeping her happy without further harassment but despite being brought back on 18.11.2013, the respondents repeated their behaviour and on Smt. Lalita vs Sh. Pawan Kumar on 7 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163182144/ 2 10.05.2015 when the respondent no.1 tried to strangle her, respondent (mother in law) caught hold of her hands and respondent no.2 (father in law), brother in law and sister in law also helped and respondent no.1 assaulted her with "Thapki" (wooden bat) on her head and back causing her injuries. She left the matrimonial house on 12.05.2014 and got an MLC done. 6. She has stated that since 12.05.2014, she has been living at the house of her parents, does not have any source of income, is dependent on her parents, with three sisters and her father being the only earning member whereas the respondents no.1 has own house and earns more than Rs. 15,000/ per month from private job. 7. She has also stated that she made complaint to the CAW Cel September, 2014 upon which FIR no. 664/14 was registered at PS San Vihar. She has also stated that she suffered a miscarriage due to beatings by respondents who has also threatened to kill her and kidnap her younger sisters CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors. Page 3 o if she makes a complaint. She has further stated that sometimes the respondent no.1 comes to her parents house and abuses her parents and sisters due to which she is frightened . 8. The aggrieved has stated that the respondents have refused to maintain her nor have given her any financial security and that all her jewellery and stridhen, gifts and all other household articles given by the family, friends and relatives are in possession of the respondents and as she has been constantly subjected to various forms of domestic violence, hence the present case. 9. After being served with the notice of the application, the respondents filed their reply wherein they stated that the aggrieved concealed material facts misrepresenting the same and had not approached the court with clean hands. Smt. Lalita vs Sh. Pawan Kumar on 7 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163182144/ 3 They did not deny the factum of marriage of aggrieved and respondent no.1, though, agitated that the respondent no. 2 and 3 are residing separately from them at D107, JJ Camp, Tigri, New Delhi. The maintainability of the case has been challenged due to lack of domestic relationship at the time of filing of application as also because she is stated to have deserted the respondent no.1 herself. It has been asserted that the present application has been filed only to extort money. All the allegations of the aggrieved in respect of infliction of domestic violence have been denied and it has been stated that it is aggrieved who has refused to join the company of the respondent no. 1 and that s herself is earning and is capable for sustaining herself. Rest of the averments have been denied on merits. 10. Domestic Incident Report was duly called for and was filed b CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors. Page 4 Protection Officer on 05.05.2015. 11. After the interim relief application of the aggrieved was decided, parties were referred for mediation on 17.08.2015 but matter could not be settled there and it was stated that the respondents were not appearing in media Thereafter as none appeared on behalf of respondents, respondent no.1 to 3 were proceeded exparte vide order dated 09.03.2016. 12. To prove her case, the aggrieved led exparte complainant evidence and examined only herself to prove her case. As CW1, the aggrieved Smt. Lalita tendered her evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. CW1/A) on similar lines as her application and also relied upon the following documents i.e. copy of her Adhar Card (Ex.CW1/1), copy of her marriage certificate (Ex.CW1/2A), marriage Photographs (Ex.CW1/2B), copy of the list of articles (Mark CW1/2), copy of the settlement before Mahila Panchayat (Mark CW1/3), copy of medical documents (Ex.CW1/4), copy of complaint filed before CAW Cell in May 2014 Smt. Lalita vs Sh. Pawan Kumar on 7 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163182144/ 4 (Ex.CW 1/5), copy of FIR no. 664/14, PS Sangam Vihar (Ex.CW1/6). 13. 14. By virtue of Section 2(a), the reliefs under the Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 can be availed by a woman only if she is in a domestic relationship with the respondent and was subjected to dom violence by the respondent. 15. From the unrebutted testimony of CW1 and the documents Ex CW1/2A, CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors. Page 5 of Ex CW1/2B the marriage of the aggrieved with the respondent no.1 13.03.2013 stands duly proved even more so as the same has not been disputed by the respondents in their reply. The aggrieved as CW1 has further testified that thereafter she resided with the respondents at the house of the respondent no.1 with all the respondents. Though the respondent no. 2 and 3 took a plea in their reply as to them residing separately from the aggrieved and the respondent no.1, as they were proceeded exparte, they failed to defend their case and to lead any evidence in support of their plea as raised in their defence to prove the same. Thus, no rebuttal has come against the claims of the aggrieved. The oral testimony of CW1 and has not been traversed and the testimony of CW1 goes unrebutted and unchallenged. No reason has been brought on record t disbelieve the unrebutted and uncontroverted evidence led by the aggrieved. Hence the factum of existence of shared household of the aggrieved and the respondents has been proved.
texts.arguments: 16. In respect of existence of shared household a plea had been raised in the reply of the respondents that as at the time of filing of the com Smt. Lalita vs Sh. Pawan Kumar on 7 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163182144/ 5 aggrieved was not residing under domestic relationship with the respondent, hence there was no relationship which was alive at that time hence ingredient remained unfulfilled. However, the plea as raised is legall tenable as in the instant case as per the unrebutted testimony of the aggrieved she was constrained to leave her shared household due to the infli domestic violence by the respondents and not out of her own volition. Further it is duly noted that merely because the aggrieved was not living wit CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors. Pa respondents at the time of the filing of the application/complaint cannot be said to result in the domestic relationship ceasing because such restrictiv interpretation if adopted would imply that for the aggrieved to be able to avail the remedies provided under this Act, she must continue to suffer and reside in the same place where she is being subjected to violence which is contrary to the beneficial object of the Act. 17. Further the reliance placed on the judgments by the respondents in their reply is also misguided for the reason that the judgment of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Harbans Lal Malik v Payal Malik (2010) as also in the case of Vijay Sharma v State of NCT (2010) are distinguishable as to the facts of the case. It is duly noted that as the marriage between the aggrieved has not been dissolved as on date, the domestic relationship between them cannot be said to have ceased. Further as the respondent no.2 and 3 have not led any evidence to prove that they were residing separately from the aggrieved the proceedings nor to controvert any evidence led by the aggrieved . Thu averments of the aggrieved as also her testimony in her evidence by way of affidavit in respect of infliction of various forms of domestic viol CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors. Page 7 including physical, verbal and economic abuse are deemed to be admitted by the respondents as they have remained unchallenged and unrebutted. Further, no reason has been brought on record to disbelieve the uncontroverted evidence led by the aggrieved. Accordingly, by unrebutted testimony, the aggrieved has been able to prove that the respondents have committed certain acts of domestic violence and as she has been able to prove the domestic violence committed upon her by the respondents, she is entitled to claim reliefs under the Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against all the respondents. Reliefs 19. Protection Order Under Section 18 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act: Aggrieved has sought the following reliefs: i) Prohibiting acts of domestic violence by granting an injunction against the respondents from repeating any of the acts mentioned in terms of column 4(a)/(b)/(c)/(d)/(e)(f)(g) of the application. ii) Prohibiting the respondent from committing any act of domestic violence against her iii) Prohibiting the respondent from aiding or abetting in the commission of acts of domestic violence; iv) Prohibiting from alienating jewellery, ornaments and articles of complainant by the respondent including her stridhan or any other property held either jointly by the parties or separately by them without the leave of the Magistrate; v) Prohibiting from committing any other act as specified in the protection order. 20. of domestic violence as deposed to by the aggrieved as also committing any acts of domestic violence or aiding or abetting the same. 22. Residence Order Under Section 19 of Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act: The aggrieved has prayed for the following residence orders: i) pass a residence order directing the respondents to secure same level of alternate accommodation for the complainant as enjoyed by her in the shared household or to pay rent for the same, if the circumstances so require; ii) impose any additional conditions or pass any other direction which he may deem reasonably necessary to protect or to provide for the safety of the complainant; iii) direct the respondents to execute a bond, with or without sureties, for preventing the commission of domestic violence; and also iv) direct the officer in charge of the nearest police station to give protection to the complainant; v) impose on the respondents obligations relating to the discharge of rent CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors. Page 9 of 14 and other payments, having regard to the financial needs and resources of the parties. 33. The default shall be viewed in terms of the judgment of Hon'ble High Court in Gaurav Sondhi Vs. Divya Sondhi-120 DLT(2005)426.
